question.worked_solution:
We start by recalling the conversion table for mass units. 

| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kilogram | $\textrm{kg}$ | $1\,\textrm{kg} = 1\,000\,\textrm{g}$ |
| Gram | $\textrm{g}$ | Base Unit |
| Milligram | $\textrm{mg}$ | $1\,000\,\textrm{mg} = 1\,\textrm{g}$ |

There are $1000\,\textrm {mg}$ per $\textrm{g},$ which we can write as follows:

$$
\dfrac{1000\,\textrm{mg}}{\textrm{g}}
$$

This is our conversion factor.

Now, multiplying $2.25 \,\textrm{g}$ by our conversion factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2.25\,\text{g} & =2.25\,\text{g}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\text{g}} \\  & =2.25\,\cancel{\text{g}}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\cancel{\text{g}}} \\  & =2.25\cdot 1\,000\,\text{mg} \\  & =2\,250\,\text{mg}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $2.25 \,\textrm{g}$ is equivalent to $2\,250\,\text{mg}.$
